title: Literature Focus Section 4: Pride and Prejudice True/False and Comprehension Questions on Mr Wickham and Mr Darcy
summary: Activities based on an extract from Pride and Prejudice: students judge statements as true or false and answer comprehension questions about Mr Wickham's claims regarding Mr Darcy's father's will and Elizabeth's reactions.

title: Vocabulary Matching, Sentence Completion, and Creative Writing on Pride and Prejudice Extract
summary: Students find words matching given definitions, complete sentences using vocabulary from Exercise C with word form changes, and imagine writing a letter from the late Mr Darcy explaining his will's terms.

title: Literature Focus Section 5: Pride and Prejudice Multiple Choice and True/False on Elizabeth and Mr Darcy's Conversation
summary: Multiple-choice and true/false exercises on an extract from Pride and Prejudice focusing on Elizabeth's dislike of Mr Darcy, his proposal, and their exchange about Mr Wickham.

title: Comprehension, Vocabulary Matching, and Creative Letter Writing on Pride and Prejudice Extract
summary: Students answer questions about Mr Darcy's reaction to Elizabeth discussing Mr Wickham, find synonyms for given meanings, and write a letter from Elizabeth to Mr Wickham about Mr Darcy's proposal.

title: Literature Focus Section 6: Pride and Prejudice Sequencing Events and Comprehension Questions
summary: Students order key events from an extract from Pride and Prejudice in chronological order and answer questions about Mr Darcy and Elizabeth's conversation regarding Lady Catherine's visit and their changing feelings.

title: Vocabulary Exercises and Creative Letter Writing from Mr Darcy to His Aunt in Pride and Prejudice
summary: Students find words matching given meanings, fill in sentences using vocabulary from Exercise C with necessary word changes, and write a letter as Mr Darcy informing his aunt of his engagement to Elizabeth Bennet.

title: Literature Focus Section 1: As You Like It Sequencing, Comprehension, and Character Matching Activities
summary: Activities based on extracts from As You Like It: students order events involving Orlando and Oliver, answer comprehension questions, and match characters with their descriptive features.

title: Old English Vocabulary Comparison and Creative Writing about the Fight in As You Like It
summary: Students compare original and modern English extracts to identify equivalent old English words, then write a short paragraph predicting what happens next with Charles and Orlando's fight.
